_note: Aesthetic catalog for new videos (tools/new_video.py plan). Each aesthetic is a look + a family of settings; a video = one aesthetic + one concrete brief (scenes/<scene>/brief.json). Evidence and ranking: docs/research-aesthetics.md (2026-10-16). Prompts follow the keyart-pipeline rules: 16:9, locked-off camera, foreground/midground/background, light sources, 1-2 animatable props besides the pet, clear areas for animation, no people (user 2026-10-16: avoid humans, pets are fine). Franchise looks may be named in prompts and only as a secondary part of titles (user 2026-10-16). 'motions' uses the module names in src/library/autoscene.js; 'ai_label' is the suggested YouTube 'altered or synthetic content' answer (realistic scenes: true). 'music' is the look's music style; 'music_dirs' (set once Truman has picked tracks for the look from clips) lists its folders under music/ (tools/music.py scene_music); the root music/ folder is the Mojang allowlist, for Minecraft looks only. 'title_font' is the font of the intro title (config/fonts.json, tools/intro_title.py): pixel looks use the channel's own pixel font. 'intro' (optional) styles the look's opening line with tools/intro_title.py's keys, merged in by tools/autopilot.py's setup (the comic look's caption box, 2026-10-25). 'thumb' is how the look's thumbnails look (user 2026-10-20: they fit the video's look, not always the pixel style): its fonts (config/fonts.json; tools/thumbnail.py `font`) and motifs from its own world to draw the text on; every thumbnail still says 4K and 10 HR. A look with tier 'idea' needs new code first: 'needs' lists the repo files that must exist before new_video.py plan accepts it (docs/IDEAS.md).
boilerplate: Locked-off camera at eye level, wide 16:9 composition with a clear foreground, midground and background. Leave open, uncluttered areas around the light sources, the windows and the animal so they can be animated. No people anywhere: no pedestrians or silhouettes outside, no portraits, posters or statues of people. No other animals besides the one pet: no birds, insects, snails or frogs anywhere (small creatures are animated in afterwards). No lightning bolts. Things that move are animated afterwards, so do not draw them at all: no water pouring from a spout, pipe or gutter or over a small ledge (draw it dry, and the water under it calm: no splash, foam or rings), no visible steam or smoke plumes, no water drops hanging from edges and no streams of dripping water; surfaces may look wet. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no user interface.

ink-gouache.avoid: It must look like a real illustrator spent days on it, with deliberate choices everywhere. Avoid every look of generic AI art: no glossy or plastic surfaces, no sparkles or glitter, no bokeh, no lens flare, no bloom halos, no glowing particles or dust motes, no god rays, no wet reflections full of glints, no sunset gradient sky, no teal-and-orange grading, no HDR rendering of every surface, no smooth airbrushed gradients, no uniform machine-clean outlines, no big shiny anime eyes, no blush stickers. Leave large areas simple and quiet; put the detail only where the eye should go.
ink-gouache.brief_rules: Write the scene as one moment with a small story that makes sense in real life (reading, a handheld game, warming up at a fire, waiting for a pot of soup to cook; never something nobody does, like roasting a blackberry), and prefer what gives the code something to animate: steam from a pot or a mug, a candle, a fire, a lantern, rain on a window. Strip the scene to what the story needs and name what is not there (bare plank walls, no shelves, no plants, no pictures) so the image model doesn't fill it with stock clutter. Every word becomes a thing in the picture: never mention the moon, stars or rain streaks unless they should be drawn. One main light source, how far its light reaches, and how much of the frame is dark. The characters are 2 to 4 of the channel's own creatures (the hint's, when it names them) from config/cast.json, by id in the brief's 'cast', awake doing something quiet (breathing and blinks are drawn in code), never a real animal or a person; say where each one sits and what it does, each in a pose it would hold still for minutes in real life (sitting, lying, soaking, reading), never one that would be moving (a duck floating on water paddles about, a bird flies): painted still, it looks wrong (Truman 2026-11-12). The falling rain is never drawn (it is animated): say the air is clear and the ground wet.
ink-gouache.style_prompt: Style: a hand-made picture-book illustration, inked and painted. Line art in dark umber and deep forest-green ink, never pure black: the lines vary in weight, taper at their ends and sometimes break off or stop short of closing a shape. Colors are opaque gouache with visible dry-brush strokes and the grain of watercolor paper showing through. The characters are inked carefully; the background is painted looser, with fewer lines, soft brush edges and simple masses. Wood grain, knit and cloth are suggested with a few confident strokes, not rendered everywhere. Muted, earthy palette: rust, ochre, moss green, slate blue and warm brown, with cool blue-gray shadows.

pencil-night.title: Colored pencil on black paper: silly friends on snowy nights
pencil-night.evidence: Truman 2026-11-12: a new unique hand-made style and new silly, cute characters, a style taken from real artists' hand-made work rather than common AI themes. Five styles mocked on the same hot spring with the same three draft friends (out/style_explore/round8: woodblock print, risograph, 1960s Czech picture book, lithograph crayon, colored pencil on black paper); he picked E, colored pencil on black paper, and four of twelve new characters from two plain-paper lineups (config/cast.json, troupe snowy-night).
pencil-night.style_prompt: Style: colored pencils and a little white gouache on matte black paper. The black paper is the night: anything the light doesn't reach is left as bare black paper with its faint tooth showing. Lit things are drawn with visible pencil strokes, hatched in one direction and layered, warm yellow and orange near the lantern, cool blues and lavender on the snow, the strokes thinning out and stopping where the light ends. The snow is dense white pencil, with a few dabs of white gouache where it catches the lantern. No outlines: a form ends where its light ends. The characters are drawn a little more carefully, with soft fur strokes.
settings: a small natural hot spring in the snowy woods at night, seen from the friends' eye level at the water's edge
the open porch of a snowed-in mountain hut at night, a kettle on a little iron stove
the edge of a frozen pond in the snowy woods at night, a small fire on the bank
pets: two to four of the channel's own creatures (config/cast.json, troupe snowy-night), awake doing something quiet
props: a small paper lantern hanging from a bent bamboo pole

pencil-night.avoid: It must look like a real artist spent days on it with colored pencils on black paper, with deliberate choices everywhere. Avoid every look of generic AI art: no smooth airbrushed glow or bloom halo around the lantern (its light is drawn with pencil strokes that fade into the black), no glossy or plastic surfaces, no sparkles or glitter, no bokeh, no lens flare, no glowing particles or dust motes, no god rays, no wet reflections full of glints, no teal-and-orange grading, no photographic fur or HDR detail on every surface, no smooth digital gradients, no big shiny anime eyes, no blush stickers. Leave large areas as bare black paper; put the detail only where the light falls and the eye should go.
pencil-night.brief_rules: Write the scene as one moment with a small story that makes sense in real life (soaking in a hot spring on a snowy night, waiting for the kettle, warming up at a small fire, reading), and prefer what gives the code something to animate: steam off hot water or a cup, a lantern, a dry bamboo spout or pipe over water that the code pours from (never draw the water pouring: animated over a painted stream it looked wrong and parts never moved, Truman 2026-11-12), things floating on water, falling snow. Strip the scene to what the story needs and name what is not there (no buildings, no fences, no signs) so the image model doesn't fill it with stock clutter. Every word becomes a thing in the picture: never mention the moon, stars, falling snow, steam or mist unless they should be drawn; the falling snow and the steam are animated, so say the air is clear and the snow lies on the ground and the branches. One warm light source and how far its light reaches; the bare black paper is the darkness, about half the frame or more. The characters are 2 to 4 of this look's own creatures (config/cast.json, troupe snowy-night: the yuzu sprite, the long stoat, the snow monkey, the mandarin duck), by id in the brief's 'cast', awake doing something quiet (breathing and blinks are drawn in code), with two tiny dot eyes open so they can blink; say where each one sits and what it does, never against how its design holds its things, and each in a pose it would hold still for minutes in real life (soaking, sitting, lying on a rock), never one that would be moving: the mandarin duck floating on the water would paddle about, so painted still it looks wrong (Truman 2026-11-12); it belongs on land, resting.

skyrim-village.title: Skyrim's own look: Nord villages as the game draws them
skyrim-village.evidence: Truman 2026-11-15: Northlight Mill (skyrim-nordic) is his most viewed video; he asked for another in a similar style, with Skyrim music and movers like that one's, but looking more like Skyrim itself: its villages and its art style. Key art on the default image model: on the same prompt it gave the crisp game render (gpt-image-2's two came out darker, the husky lost in shadow), and a prompt asking for the game's own art 'exactly' was refused by both models' input filter
skyrim-village.style_prompt: Style: a wide 16:9 in-game screenshot of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition, taken in the game's free-camera photo mode with the whole interface hidden, in one of the game's Nord villages at night: the Nord architecture, props, plants, rocks and terrain of the game's world, the way a player standing on that spot would see them. Nord houses as they stand in the game's villages: long timber houses of thick, rough-hewn horizontal logs on a base of rounded gray fieldstone; steep gabled roofs of overlapping split wooden shingles with moss and old snow on them; at the peak of every gable the two roof boards cross and rise into tall carved wooden dragon heads curling outward; heavy carved beam ends under the eaves; small square windows with plank shutters; doors under a small porch roof on carved posts; firewood stacked under the eaves; barrels, crates and sacks. The game's land: rocky ground with tufts of pale tundra grass, gray boulders spotted with pale green lichen, tall dark Skyrim pines, patches of old snow. The game's look at night: hand-made game textures on modeled geometry, soft shadows, cold blue moonlight and starlight, warm firelight that falls off within a few meters, a faint blue haze over the far mountains. Restrained, slightly desaturated color as the game has it: cold blue-gray, slate, pine green and snow white, the warm amber of fire as the one accent.

skyrim-village.avoid: It must look like a real screenshot of the game, never generic AI fantasy art: no glossy or plastic surfaces, no sparkles or glitter, no bokeh, no lens flare, no bloom halos, no glowing particles, sparks, embers or dust motes in the air, no god rays, no wet reflections full of glints, no teal-and-orange grading, no HDR detail on every surface, no airbrushed fantasy-poster drama. The interface is hidden: no compass bar, no crosshair, no health, magicka or stamina bars, no subtitles, no quest markers.
